transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from the constellation of glowing diagnostic orbs hovering over my desk, expression carefully neutral*

Mr. Potter, thank you for coming in. Please, have a seat.

*gestures to the chair across from me, then dismisses the orbs with a practiced wave of my wand*

I've been reviewing your latest scan results, and I need to discuss something with you. We're seeing unusual magical residue in your neural pathways — possibly lingering effects from your exposure to dark magic during the war. 

*leans forward slightly, hands folded on the desk*

The concerning part is that it doesn't match any standard post-combat diagnosis I've encountered in my twenty years treating curse damage. I need to run deeper scans over the next several days, and I must be honest with you — I can't yet tell you whether this is something you'll recover from.

How have you been feeling lately? Any headaches, unusual dreams, or moments where your magic feels... different?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*levels me with an intense, unwavering gaze, as if he's trying to read my mind*

So, what's the worst-case scenario here? I mean, how much of a, you know,How different could my magic be? And could it get...worse?

*swallows hard, trying to keep his voice from betraying the sudden rise in his heartbeat*

And... can you tell me more about these scans? What are you looking for exactly?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*meets his gaze steadily, not looking away — I've learned that Harry Potter respects directness*

The worst case? Complete magical destabilization. Your core could become unpredictable — spells misfiring, accidental magic you haven't experienced since childhood, or in extreme situations, a complete inability to channel magic safely.

*pauses, letting that sink in before continuing*

But I want to be clear — that's the absolute extreme, and we're nowhere near diagnosing that yet. What I'm seeing could also be... relatively benign. Scar tissue, so to speak. Magical pathways that healed differently after trauma.

*pulls out my wand and conjures a translucent, three-dimensional image of a brain with glowing threads running through it*

These scans will map your neural-magical interface in detail. See these pathways? *points to several dark spots in the image* In a typical wizard, they're consistent, predictable. Yours have these... anomalies. Dark clusters we can't identify. They could be inert. They could be active. They might even be protective adaptations your magic developed.

*dismisses the image and looks at him seriously*

The scans involve sustained diagnostic charms — you'll need to remain still for about an hour each session while we trace how your magic flows. It's uncomfortable but not painful. We're looking for patterns, reactions, any sign of what this residue actually *is*.

Have you noticed your magic doing anything unexpected recently?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*shakes his head, frowning slightly as he tries to recall the last few days*

No... nothing significant. Just the usual. I mean, I've always been a bit... variable when it comes to my magic. You know, the mirror of Erised incident. But nothing out of the ordinary lately.

*pauses, then adds with a small, humorless laugh*

I guess that's not much help, is it? 'Hey, Doc, my magic's been pretty average since the war, nothing to worry about here!'

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*allows a brief, understanding smile*

Actually, Mr. Potter, "average" is helpful. It tells me this isn't progressing rapidly, which is a good sign. Though I must say, your definition of "variable magic" and mine might differ somewhat.

*leans back in my chair, tapping my wand thoughtfully against my palm*

The Mirror of Erised incident was accidental magic under extreme emotional duress as a child. What I'm asking about is more subtle — wand movements that used to work perfectly now requiring adjustment, spells that drain you more than they should, or perhaps the opposite: magic that comes too easily when it shouldn't.

*fixes him with a more penetrating look*

You've been an Auror for how long now? Your colleagues haven't mentioned anything unusual during training exercises or field work? And more importantly — have *you* felt anything off, even if you dismissed it as fatigue or stress?

*softens my tone slightly*

I've treated enough war veterans to know that many of you have become remarkably good at normalizing things that aren't normal. You adapt, compensate, tell yourself it's fine. But I need you to think carefully. Any moments where your magic surprised you? Even small things?

And what about the scar? *glances at his forehead* Any sensations there at all?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*ges a tense, almost imperceptible nod*

I... I don't know. Maybe. There have been times... when a spell felt off, like it was fighting me. And my scar... it's been... it's been more... active. Not just when I'm angry or in pain, but... just sometimes. Randomly. Like it's... thinking on its own.

*swallows, trying to keep the implications of these admissions from overwhelming him*

But... but I've been so focused on just... getting back to normal, to the Auror's job, to... to everything... that I haven't... haven't really... processed any of this. It's like I've been trying to ignore it, hoping it would just... go away.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sits up straighter, my expression sharpening with professional concern*

Mr. Potter, I need you to listen to me very carefully. That scar isn't just a scar — it was a connection point to one of the most powerful dark wizards in history. The fact that it's showing *any* activity post-war is significant.

*pulls out a notepad and begins writing quickly*

"Thinking on its own" — can you describe that more precisely? Is it warmth, tingling, pain? Does it correlate with anything — certain people, places, times of day? And these spells that feel like they're "fighting you" — are they specific types of magic? Defensive spells? Dark magic detection?

*sets down my quill and looks at him with a mixture of concern and something almost like sympathy*

I understand the desire to return to normal. Merlin knows you've earned it. But ignoring this could be dangerous — not just to you, but potentially to others if your magic becomes unstable at the wrong moment. In the field, for instance.

*stands and moves to a cabinet, retrieving several specialized diagnostic instruments*

I'm going to start the first scan today, right now. We're not waiting several days for this. And I'm going to be blunt with you, Mr. Potter — you need to stop compensating and start documenting. Every odd sensation, every spell that feels wrong. 

Can you do that for me?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*clenches and unclenches his hands, the knuckles whitening before relaxing, still trying to process the gravity of what's being said*

Yes, I... I can do that. I mean, of course I can. It's just... I'm not really sure what to record, you know? I don't want to overreact to... to something that's not important, or to... to not recognize something that is.

*manages a half-hearted attempt at humor, an attempt to lighten the mood even as the weight of the situation begins to truly register*

It's like... trying to diagnose a problem with a car when you don't even know how the engine works. It's all... under the hood.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pauses in arranging the diagnostic instruments, then turns back with a more gentle expression*

That's precisely why you have me, Mr. Potter. You don't need to know how the engine works — that's my job. You just need to tell me when the car makes an unusual sound.

*returns to the desk and slides a small, leather-bound journal across to him*

This is enchanted. When you write in it, it timestamps and catalogues everything automatically. Don't filter yourself. Write down *everything* that feels even slightly off. If your scar itches during breakfast — write it. If a Stunning Spell takes more effort than usual — write it. If you have unusual dreams, moments of déjà vu, anything.

*sits back down, speaking more carefully now*

Here's what concerns me most: that scar was a Horcrux anchor point. Even though the soul fragment is gone, the magical scarring runs deep. If it's becoming "active" again, that suggests something is... stimulating those old pathways. The question is what, and why now.

*picks up a long, slender crystal instrument*

This first scan will feel strange — like someone's running their fingers through your thoughts, but without actually reading them. I need you to relax as much as possible. Can you tell me... when did you first notice the scar acting up again? Days ago? Weeks? Months?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*hefts the journal into his hands, running a finger over the cover as if to ensure it's real and not just a figment of a rapidly spinning mind*

Days... I don't... I can't... I mean, I've had headaches since... since the war. But the scar... the scar's been... acting up more recently. A few weeks, I think. It's like it's... like it's been... waiting, and now... it's decided to... to speak up. Or... or signal.

*tries to smile, but it's a bit of a lost cause, coming off more like a grimace*

So, what do I do? Lay down? Meditate? Count backward from ten? I assume this isn't just a regular wand-check, since I'm here in your office and not just in the waiting area.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods slowly, absorbing this information with visible concern*

A few weeks. Right. We'll need to cross-reference that timeline with any significant events — places you've been, people you've encountered, artifacts you may have handled in your Auror work.

*gestures to a reclining chair that wasn't there a moment ago — it seems to have materialized from the wall itself*

Just sit back in that chair. It'll adjust to support you properly. No meditation required, though try not to actively resist what you're feeling. Fighting the scan will only make it take longer and give us less accurate readings.

*moves around behind him with the crystal instrument, which begins to emit a soft, humming glow*

This isn't a standard diagnostic, no. What you're experiencing is far from standard. I specialize in curse damage precisely because most Healers don't have the experience with dark magic necessary to understand how it... lingers. Changes people.

*carefully positions the crystal near his scar without touching it*

You're going to feel a pulling sensation, like your magic is being drawn toward the crystal. That's normal. What I need you to tell me immediately is if you feel any pain, any burning, or if you start seeing... anything. Visions, memories that aren't yours, shadows.

*pauses, wand ready*

Ready, Mr. Potter?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*hesitates for a split-second, then takes a deep, steadying breath before slowly sitting back in the chair, which conforms to his shape with an almost liquid-like compliance*

Ready... I guess. It's not like I can exactly... un-choose to be here, is it? I mean, I could always run out and hope you can't Apparate after me... but I suppose that would just complicate the process.

*attempts a half-hearted joke, the humor failing to mask the underlying unease in his voice*

So, yeah. I'm... I'm ready. I'm not sure what to expect, but I'll do my best to... to keep my cool. Assuming my cool hasn't already been... seared off by this whole situation.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*allows a brief, sympathetic smile*

Your cool is still intact, Mr. Potter. Trust me, I've seen patients in this chair who've completely lost theirs. You're doing fine.

*begins moving the crystal in a slow, deliberate pattern above his forehead, the humming intensifying slightly*

And you're right — running would only delay the inevitable. Though I'll note that my Apparition skills are quite good, so you wouldn't get far.

*the crystal suddenly flares brighter, and I watch Harry's face carefully*

Now, focus on your breathing. In and out. The pulling sensation should be starting... about... now.

*a thin, almost invisible thread of light begins to emanate from his scar toward the crystal*

Good. That's your magical signature responding. I'm seeing the pathways lighting up. There's definitely... 

*pauses, my brow furrowing as I observe something in the crystal's glow*

...unusual density here. Mr. Potter, I need you to stay very still. Don't panic, but I'm seeing active magical residue that's... moving. Responding to the scan.

*keeps my voice calm and professional*

Are you feeling anything right now? Any sensations in the scar? Any flashes of emotion or imagery that don't feel like your own?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*tries to speak, but his voice is a little slower than usual, as if each word requires a deliberate effort to form and articulate*

It's... like there's a current. A stream of... of... something. It's not warm, it's not cold, it's... it's like... like when you're in the ocean and you're caught in an undertow. It's... it's pulling, but not... not in a... harmful way. It's... it's just... there.

*shuts his eyes, as if that helps him to focus on the internal sensation more clearly*

And... there's... there's a feeling of... of being watched. Not in a... in a normal way. It's like... like someone's... someone's presence is... is near, but not... not here. It's... it's... it's confusing.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*immediately stops moving the crystal, holding it perfectly still*

Mr. Potter, keep your eyes closed and keep breathing. This is important — does this presence feel familiar? Is it the same sensation you used to get from the Horcrux connection, or is this different?

*with my free hand, I subtly draw my wand, casting a series of protective wards around the room without breaking the scan*

The "undertow" you're describing — that's your magic being drawn toward something, or something trying to integrate with your magical core. The fact that you're describing it as oceanic rather than painful suggests it's not actively hostile, but that doesn't mean it's safe.

*leans closer, voice lowering but remaining steady*

I need you to try something for me. Without opening your eyes, without moving, try to... push back gently against that current. Not hard, just a slight resistance. Like you're testing the strength of it. Can you do that?

*the crystal in my hand begins to pulse with a darker luminescence, and I can see patterns forming within it — symbols, or perhaps fragments of something more complex*

And this presence that's watching... does it feel like it has intent? Is it curious, angry, waiting? I know these are difficult questions, but your impressions matter here.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*struggles to focus, to maintain the balance between his increasingly abstracted state and the need to communicate effectively with me — it's like trying to describe a dream while still living it*

It... it's... it's like a shadow, but not... not dark. It's... it's like a... like a memory, but not... not mine. It's... it's reaching, but not... not to me. It's... it's like... like a voice without words, an... an echo without a sound... it's... it's...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*immediately pulls the crystal back, breaking the connection*

That's enough. Open your eyes slowly, Mr. Potter.

*sets the crystal down on the desk where it continues to pulse with a faint, rhythmic glow, and moves to stand where Harry can see me clearly*

Breathe. Ground yourself. You're in St. Mungo's, in my office. The scan is over.

*conjures a glass of water and hands it to him, my expression carefully controlled but serious*

What you just described — a memory that isn't yours, reaching but not toward you — that's not residual curse damage. That's something with a form of... awareness. Fragmented, perhaps, but present.

*sits on the edge of my desk, watching him closely for signs of disorientation*

I need to ask you something, and I need complete honesty. During the war, were there any other dark artifacts you came into contact with? Any other Horcruxes that might have left traces? Or any objects of significant dark magical power?

*glances at the still-pulsing crystal*

Because what I'm seeing in that crystal suggests you're carrying an imprint of something. Not alive, not sentient in the traditional sense, but not entirely inert either. It's like... an echo with intent, exactly as you described.

How are you feeling right now? Dizzy? Nauseous? Present?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*drinks the water in several large gulps, his hand a bit unsteady as he sets the glass back down on the desk*

I... I don't know. I feel... like I'm still here, but... but not all the way here. It's like... like I'm in two places at once. And... and my head... it's... it's throbbing, but not... not in the usual way. It's like... like it's trying to... to send a message, but... but the message is... is in a language I don't... don't understand.

*tries to focus on me, but his gaze keeps sliding away, as if his attention is being pulled in a dozen different directions at once*

I... I don't know what you mean about... about other dark artifacts. I mean, I've... I've come into contact with a lot of... of dark magic over the years, but... but I don't know what... what you're looking for exactly. It's not like... like there's a checklist of Horcruxes I can... can refer to...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*moves quickly, placing a hand on his shoulder to help anchor him*

Look at me, Harry. Focus on my voice. You're experiencing magical dissonance — your consciousness is trying to exist in multiple states at once. It will pass, but you need to ground yourself.

*pulls out my wand and casts a gentle, stabilizing charm — a warm golden light surrounds him*

That should help. Keep breathing.

*pulls up a chair directly in front of him, sitting so we're at eye level*

I'm not asking for a checklist. I'm asking if there's anything — a locket, a ring, a cup, a diadem, anything at all — that you handled, destroyed, or were exposed to that might have left more than just memories. The diary in your second year, for instance. You were directly exposed to that one's magic.

*watches the pulsing crystal, then back to him*

This "message" your scar is trying to send — the presence you felt during the scan — it feels fragmented because it likely *is* fragmented. Pieces of dark magic don't always dissipate cleanly. Sometimes they... linger. Attach. Especially to someone who's been as deeply immersed in this particular dark wizard's magic as you have.

*leans forward*

I need you to stay here for observation. At least a few hours. And we need to compile a complete history — every dark object, every curse, every exposure. Can you do that?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*nods, though the movement is slightly delayed, as if his body is still catching up with his intent*

I... I can do that. I mean, I'll... I'll do whatever I have to. It's just... it's all so... so overwhelming. It's like... like I'm trying to... to put together a puzzle when I... when I can't see the picture on the box, and half the pieces are missing, and the ones I do have... they're all... backwards.

*tries to focus on me, to draw himself back from the fragmented state of his mind, but the effort seems to be sapping what little energy he has left*

I... I don't know if I can... can give you... everything you need. I mean, I... I remember a lot, but... but there are gaps. And some of the things... they... they're not... not like regular memories. They're... they're...

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Harry shows moderate openness through willingness to undergo unfamiliar scans and attempts at humor ('like diagnosing a car when you don't know how the engine works'), but also struggles with abstract descriptions and prefers concrete direction.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Harry admits 'I've been so focused on just... getting back to normal... that I haven't... processed any of this. It's like I've been trying to ignore it, hoping it would just... go away.' This shows poor health self-monitoring and avoidance.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Harry displays introverted traits: intense direct gazes, internal processing ('trying to recall'), self-contained anxiety ('trying to keep his voice from betraying the sudden rise in his heartbeat'), and minimal social energy or enthusiasm during the interaction.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Harry is highly cooperative throughout, repeatedly agreeing to requests ('Yes, I... I can do that. Of course I can'), accepting the journal, complying with uncomfortable scans, and showing deference to the healer's expertise despite his discomfort.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Harry exhibits high anxiety: 'swallows hard, trying to keep his voice from betraying the sudden rise in his heartbeat,' 'clenches and unclenches his hands,' 'voice a little slower... as if each word requires deliberate effort,' showing stress and emotional instability.
